newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close up strongly led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close up strongly led by banks.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Tuesday for the third consecutive day led by a rise in bank stocks, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 2.10 percent, or 5.56 points, to 270.57 on a very high all-share turnover of 233 million shekels against 218 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.13 percent higher at 277.73.
"The market is very strong and it is expected to continue rising. There are very few sellers and the public is still outside looking to get in," said Amir Eayal of Epsilon Securities.
"The market doesn't stop. Activity is growing and new money is coming in," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank. "Bank shares led the market's rise."
Traders said bank stocks rose after Finance Minister Dan Meridor on Monday proposed criteria for the state-controlled "arrangement" banks to begin paying dividends.

Under the proposals, which were discussed with the heads of the three main banks in government hands, the banks will pay dividends on the sale of non-bank companies they have been forced to sell as part of the government's bank-reform law.

Traders said the mood in the market is very bullish. "I don't believe that we will see a real correction in the near future because investors are looking for every opportunity to buy stocks," Eayal said.
"We might see some profit-taking in the short run but the positive trend will continue," the Mizrahi trader added.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which surged 3.75 percent to 702 agorot on volume of 11 million shekels; Israel Discount Bank, which gained 1.5 percent to 378 agorot on turnover of 10.5 million shekels; and Bank Leumi which surged 5.0 percent to 560 agorot on volume of 9.5 million shekels.
